body:
A private Lavapipe Endpoint prototype now evaluates each ray with one invocation. Inter-invocation barriers and atomic status updates are omitted only under an explicit compile-time one-invocation guard; the arithmetic, original general/Schwarzschild programs, descriptor layout and row words are preserved. Actual loaded-module → ordinary LLVM passes → called-code/relocation joins show that the stock coroutine is gone. Executable code grows from 922,597 to 973,131 bytes; this is a structural finding, not a speedup claim.

The unchanged original `FactoredEndpointsPreserveIndependentRootsAndBoundaryAdmission` prerequisite passes in 118.108 seconds under its original 300-second/4-GiB/2-GiB guard. All four original normal/integer and default/FP64-product routes ran, with zero failures/errors/skips/disabled cases and 56 complete active-row readback digests. The original 29 factor rows/30 root alternatives, 27 additional rows/23 required admissions, test objects, numerical assertions, refusal/recovery and reordered/shrinking-prefix checks are retained. Actual selected normal-module hashes match the prototype; conservative integer fallback modules remain unchanged.

This is an unadopted, Endpoint-only prototype: 1/8 original controls completed, no original benefit trial or frame attempted, and no full scientific/runtime/release claim. Remaining integrated controls and all unchanged benefit gates are still required before adoption. [Complete pushed private sources, called-code captures, exact executable and original control evidence](https://github.com/sunyaisblank/Sirius/tree/7e6e97a3e1305c88650cf266f6350a33b534474d/attestations/qualification/630844e7/software-single-invocation-endpoint). Canonical development remains clean and pushed at 630844e7; PR62 stays draft and unmerged.
